tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Digital Design Tools and Techniques

questions.question: Create a series of experimental studies exploring digital design tools and techniques. Annotate your process.
questions.correctAnswer: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to digital design tools and techniques, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refined outcomes.

questions.question: Research an artist or designer who works with digital design tools and techniques. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work.
questions.correctAnswer: A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work.

questions.question: Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with digital design tools and techniques. Which approaches were most successful and why?
questions.correctAnswer: A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

tests.name: Extended Practice
tests.description: Self-marked extended answers on Digital Design Tools and Techniques

questions.question: Full-Mark Response Use both vector and raster software to develop a design project. Show how you combine tools and techniques, annotate your workflow, and explain why each tool was appropriate for each task. <div class="
questions.correctAnswer: A grade 9 response will: demonstrate competent use of multiple software tools; explain why each tool was chosen; show a professional workflow; annotate with technical vocabulary (paths, masks, layers, vectors, resolution). Mark scheme: AO1 (develop through investigation) + AO2 (refine through experimentation) + AO3 (record ideas and observations) + AO4 (present personal response) = total marks
questions.explanation: Extended answer: aim for the mark-scheme points, in order, with the command word addressed.
